label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae I q.44 a.1…: Mathematical things are abstract in reason, not in…
locator: I q.44 a.1 ad 3, mathematica accipiuntur ut abstracta secundum rationem through causa agente
interpretation: Preserve the respect distinction between intellectual abstraction and esse. Do not identify mathematical propositions with efficient effects, posit separately subsisting mathematical objects by default or derive necessary-being actuality from an unconstrained modal predicate. The reply is source support for cause qua esse, not a formal conversion between IsAt, InAct and CausesNecessityOf. Reading is based on the verified complete Latin article and its objections/replies; no formal proof or independent premise truth is registered.
